scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. Your client's return was accepted. Years later, can the tax officer reopen it, or is that a mere change of opinion?
On twenty eighth October, a Supreme Court bench of Honourable Justice J B Pardiwala and Honourable Justice K Vinod Chandran ruled.
scenes.shown: On 28 October, a Supreme Court bench of Honourable Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Honourable Justice K. Vinod Chandran ruled.

scenes.dialogue: In two thousand seven, two brothers and two other shareholders agreed to sell shares of two companies, for one hundred ninety five crore and sixty crore rupees.
scenes.shown: In 2007, two brothers and two other shareholders agreed to sell shares of two companies, for ₹195 crore and ₹60 crore.

scenes.dialogue: The brothers used the gains to buy a half share in a Delhi property, claiming Section Fifty Four F. In December twenty ten, one brother's return was accepted.
scenes.shown: The brothers used the gains to buy a half share in a Delhi property, claiming Section 54F. In December 2010, one brother's return was accepted.

scenes.dialogue: Later, a tax investigation report found the shares prima facie overvalued. Then, in March twenty fifteen, reopening notices were issued.
scenes.shown: Later, a tax investigation report found the shares prima facie overvalued. Then, in March 2015, reopening notices were issued.

scenes.dialogue: The brothers argued: overvalued shares cannot mean escaped income for a seller, and reopening on the same disclosed sale is a mere change of opinion.
The Court held: reason to believe means cause or justification, tangible material with a live link to the belief. Sufficiency is not for the courts.
scenes.shown: The Court held: "reason to believe" means cause or justification, tangible material with a live link to the belief. Sufficiency is not for the courts.

scenes.dialogue: A change of opinion needs an opinion first formed. Here, one brother's assessment was a bare acceptance of his return; the other got only an intimation.
Coming after the assessment, the report was fresh material. Under the law as it stood in twenty fifteen, the notices were valid. The appeals were dismissed.
scenes.shown: Coming after the assessment, the report was fresh material. Under the law as it stood in 2015, the notices were valid. The appeals were dismissed.
